elements.content: Communication Goal: I can describe clothes using colour, size, and style adjectives.

Lesson overview:
- Level: A1 General English
- Unit: MODULE 7. CLOTHES & APPEARANCE
- Time: 60 min (Essential) / 90 min (Expanded) / 120 min (Full Workshop)
- Focus: 7.3 Describing Clothes: Colour, Size & Style
- Materials: vocabulary cards, audio, reading handout
Warm-up: say one word you already know for this topic.
Recycles clothing from Lesson 7.1.
Recycled language: size, small, medium.
Answer from memory: which word belongs to this topic?
Which word belongs to this topic?
Core Active Vocabulary (5 items):

size — how big or small clothes are. Example: What size are you?
small — little in size. Example: I would like a small skirt.
medium — between small and large. Example: I am a medium.
large — big in size. Example: The large dress is too big.
red — the colour of blood. Example: This red shirt is nice.
Essential Chunks & Functional Collocations:

• What size are you?
• I would like a ...
• It is too big.
• This style is trendy.
• Do you have it in blue?
Vocabulary practice: choose the correct word.

Which word means 'little in size'?
Complete the sentence with a word from the list.
medium is /ˈmiːdiəm/ and large is /lɑːdʒ/.
ME-dium, LARGE
Listen and repeat three times.
Which word carries the main stress?
Grammar focus: Demonstratives (this/that/these/those).
Put size, colour and style adjectives before the noun: a small red shirt, a large blue dress. Ask What size are you? and answer Medium, please.
